Essentials 2.0 · Flow inspiration · 04-recording

Recording: ideas from other products

This page shows examples from other products for the Recording module of Essentials 2.0, grouped by product. They cover starting and stopping recordings, automatic device checks, watching many rooms at once, and remote-controlled cameras that pan, tilt and zoom (PTZ) or film in 360°. They also cover announcements to the room or simulator, checking participants in, live notes and AI markers, and grading during or right after a session. The recordings library, sharing and playback are in courses/08, the debrief in 08-debrief-review, and the phone remote in 09-mobile-ipad. Sources: the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero, researched on 30 September 2026.

What we have today. LearningSpace's current session video review screen (SRV) will be reused, not rebuilt. It shows the video on the left and a panel on the right with Annotation, Data Entry, Layout and Transcript tabs. Under the video is a timeline split into colour-coded chapters, with manual and AI markers above it. Several things are planned around it. A mixer panel will have automatic safety limits. Each room gets a device self-test, run with one button or on a schedule (around 5 am), that reports 'system health OK'. A Center Overview will show many rooms. PTZ camera control will be simpler. Room audio and simulator audio become separate announcement targets. Recording can start automatically from voice, a button, the on-air light or a schedule, and the schedule can change during an event. At the end of a recording, a QR code opens the debrief on the faculty member's phone. Known problems: recording is often skipped or started by hand, and the real fix is check-in. Audio failed at 4 of the 6 centers we visited. Face recognition and identification by camera are not allowed under EU data-protection rules (GDPR).

How to read this page

Each section below is one product. Each strip of screenshots is one flow: a real sequence of screens, in the order a user sees them. Click a screenshot to enlarge it. "Worth borrowing" lists ideas we could use, and "Avoid" lists what we should not copy. Use the task filters to see only one task, and click ☆ on a flow to add it to your own shortlist.

13 products · 22 flows · 97 screens · 8 tasks

What the best products have in common

  1. A device check should end in a clear result and a fix, not a meter Preply turns the device check into a 5-second sample, a Yes/No question and a checklist, and offers 'we'll help you fix it' when the answer is No. Riverside puts 'Run test recording' next to 'Start'. VEED names the exact problem where it happens ('Your microphone is muted. Unmute') without blocking recording. Riverside's own 'An error occurred, please try again later' is the opposite: it says nothing about what failed, why, or how to retry. The per-room self-test and the mixer's safety limits should always say what failed and offer one next step.See: Preply: Testing devices · Riverside: Recording a session · VEED: Muting a microphone · Riverside: Update access
  2. Arm, count down, then make it obvious that recording is on Riverside and VEED both show a 'Starting…' countdown between the click and the 'REC' sign. VEED lets you click anywhere to cancel, and both keep Stop separate from leaving the session. After stopping, both show upload and processing progress straight away instead of going quiet. Fireflies shows the 'LIVE' status in a banner across the whole app, outside the video player, with a Stop button. That is what a control room watching several rooms needs.See: VEED: Starting a recording · Riverside: Recording a session · Fireflies: Live notes
  3. Automatic recording needs a choice of where it applies, and scheduled actions need a target Grain does more than switch auto-record on or off. It asks 'All meetings' or 'Next meeting only' and confirms with a short pop-up message, so a one-off change leaves the default alone. Slack blocks a scheduled workflow ('Needs attention') until a recipient is chosen, and every step stays editable. Essentials plans automatic recording on a schedule that can change during an event. That maps to these two examples: a default per room, an override for the next session, and no automation until a room is chosen.See: Grain: Turning on auto record · Slack: Creating a workflow
  4. One-tap markers that count themselves Riverside's 'Mark Clip' is a single button among the live recording controls. A short pop-up message shows the exact time in the recording, and the button label becomes 'Mark Clip (3)'. Fireflies lets faculty select transcript text to pin one star on the timeline, and it writes AI notes live, with a 'Catch me up (last 1 min)' button. These would feed the marker row that already exists in the SRV. The counter on the button and the single-star pin address the known problem of overlapping markers.See: Riverside: Adding a marker · Fireflies: Bookmarking a transcript · Fireflies: Live notes
  5. Grade one learner, next to the video, with evidence Grain limits a scorecard to one speaker before scoring starts and keeps it as a tab under the video. Each item allows N/A and a note, and Submit stays disabled until every item is answered. The AI version fills in the criteria with a reason and a clickable time in the video, and it says so when the call does not match. Wellfound works differently: a free-text note and a Strong Yes to Strong No scale, with no criteria and no time stamps. The SRV's Data Entry and Abbott checklist are closer to Grain, but Grain's grading window covers the video, and the SRV should avoid that.See: Grain: Scoring a speaker · Grain: Generating a scorecard · Wellfound: Adding a scorecard
  6. Checking in is how people get tagged, and undoing it takes a deliberate step Luma makes 'Check In Guests' the main action of an event: scan, confirm the person, then undo right on the confirmation screen if needed. The list shows how many are 'Going' and 'Checked In', when each person arrived, and who checked them in ('Checked In · By Sam Lee'). Partiful asks 'Uncheck them?' before reversing a check-in, with a 'Nevermind' way out. This is how to know who is in the room without biometrics, and it is the fix the baseline names for skipped recordings.See: Luma: Checking in a guest · Luma: Checking in a guest (manual check-in) · Partiful: Cancelling a check in
  7. Talking live and broadcasting a message are separate controls Alexa keeps 'Announce' apart from 'Drop In', which is a live intercom. Announce is one-way: you type, speak or pick a preset sound, then see 'Announced to all supported devices'. Slack makes push-to-talk a separate mode during a call, with an idle screen and a large hold-to-talk button that shows when the channel is open. Neither lets you choose which speaker plays the message, and that is the gap for sending audio to the room or to the simulator.See: Amazon Alexa: Creating an announcement · Slack: Turning on push-to-talk
  8. Show devices by place and room, not by device name Alexa and Google Home both group devices under room headings. They show failures right in the list ('Device is unresponsive', or an offline box with a warning triangle), so you don't have to open each device. Tesla picks cameras from dots on a diagram of the car, with a wedge showing what each camera sees. Halide cuts zoom down to three labeled levels. Together they suggest a Center Overview organized by room and a camera picker organized by position. None of them shows a live wall of many video feeds or real pan and tilt.See: Amazon Alexa: Devices · Google Home: Devices · Tesla: Live camera · Halide Mark III: Changing a focal length

Questions we still need to answer

  • Watching many rooms: no product on this page shows a live wall of many video feeds with the status of each room. Security and video-recorder apps (UniFi Protect, Verkada, Ring, Arlo, Wyze) had no usable flows on Mobbin or Refero. Alexa and Google Home show status by room, but without video. The Center Overview needs research through vendor demos, or design from first principles.
  • PTZ and 360° cameras: no flow shows panning and tilting, saved camera positions, clicking on the picture to point the camera, or flattening a 360° view. Tesla's camera map and Halide's zoom levels are the closest examples. Is 'simplified PTZ' enough if it means picking a camera by position, a few zoom levels and a handful of saved positions? That should be tested with sim techs.
  • Silent failure: no flow shows a recording that is 'on' while nothing is being captured. This page only has the good versions (VEED's muted-microphone banner, Preply's self-test) and one bad example, Riverside's vague error, which is about inviting people rather than recording. Audio failed at 4 of 6 centers, yet there is no direct reference here for an in-session 'no audio detected' check or for the mixer panel.
  • Choosing where an announcement plays: Alexa announces to 'all supported devices', and Slack's push-to-talk reaches everyone in the huddle. No product lets you choose, before speaking, whether audio goes to the room or control room, or to the simulator (the voice of the manikin). Essentials needs that.
  • Check-in as the trigger for recording is still a hypothesis. Grain ties auto-record to calendar meetings and Luma ties check-in to events, but no product links the two. Learners may not carry phones or tickets in a sim room. So Luma's fallback, switching from the scanner to a list (tapping a name, or a badge), matters as much as QR codes.
  • Grading: Grain's AI scorecard works out its criteria from patterns in sales calls, and Wellfound has no criteria at all. In simulation, rubrics are checklists that faculty own. AI evidence must respect the on-device speech-to-text and GDPR limits. No product shows a switch between formative and summative grading.

Riverside

Close match3 flows

Riverside covers the whole control-room sequence: a test recording next to 'Start', a countdown, a 'REC' sign with upload progress, and a 'Mark Clip' button that counts marks. Its vague invite error is this page's example of what not to do.

WebMobbin4 steps

Recording a session

The host opens a Riverside studio, chooses 'Start recording' or 'Run test recording', waits through a countdown, then sees live 'REC' with 'Stop', 'Mark Clip' and upload progress.

Start and stop recording, by hand or automaticallyCheck devices automatically

Worth borrowing

  • The record button offers 'Start recording' or 'Run test recording' on the same red control (screen 2).
  • A large countdown appears on the video with 'Starting…' before 'REC' begins (screen 3).
  • 'Stop' shows elapsed time (00:27) and stays separate from 'Leave' (screen 4).
  • The header shows 'REC' and upload progress, and People shows each host's upload ('720p / 93% uploaded') (screen 4).

Avoid

  • An empty 'Invite people' tile sits as large as the live feed, which competes with monitoring when starting.

What it means for Essentials Recording: models control-room start and stop outside the SRV with optional test, countdown, and 'REC' plus upload progress. 'Mark Clip' feeds the SRV timeline markers.

Adding a marker

During a live recording, the host taps 'Mark Clip' to mark a moment, a short pop-up message confirms it, and the button counts the marks so far.

Add faculty notes and automatic markers

Worth borrowing

  • One tap on 'Mark Clip' marks a moment without a form, while the 'REC' sign and upload progress stay on screen (screen 1).
  • A short pop-up message gives the exact time in the recording ('00:03:59 Clip created from marker') and can be closed (screen 2).
  • The button counts the marks so far ('Mark Clip (3)'), so the host can keep track even when marks overlap (screen 2).
  • The People panel shows how much of each participant's video has uploaded ('720p 97% uploaded') next to 'REC' (screen 1).

What it means for Essentials Recording: faculty could mark moments during a live session, and the marks would land in the existing marker row on the SRV timeline. The counter helps with the known problem of overlapping marks.

WebMobbin3 stepsExample of what not to do

Update access

The host opens 'Invite people' with link or email and roles. A red banner says 'An error occurred, please try again later' with no cause or recovery.

Tag participants on the spot, by QR check-in or automatically

Worth borrowing

  • Invite roles use plain words such as Audience, Guest, and 'Producer not recorded' (screen 2).
  • An audio-only note says 'Video won't be recorded…' and offers 'Switch to video recording' (screen 1).

Avoid

  • A generic 'An error occurred, please try again later' names no failed action, cause, or retry, so non-technical faculty cannot recover mid-session.

What it means for Essentials Recording: invite and check-in failures outside the SRV must name the action and next step, not a dismiss-only banner.

Grain

Close match3 flows

Grain is the only product that lets you choose where auto-record applies (all meetings, or just the next one). It grades one speaker at a time under the video, and its AI links each score to the moment that supports it.

WebMobbin4 steps

Turning on auto record

From the Meetings list, the user accepts a green auto-record banner, chooses 'All meetings' or 'Next meeting', sees a confirmation, and returns with the banner gone.

Start and stop recording, by hand or automatically

Worth borrowing

  • A green banner on the recording library offers one action and an X to close it (screen 1), so auto-record is visible without hunting settings.
  • The banner asks 'All meetings' or 'Next meeting only' (screen 2), so the user can set a lasting default or try one session.
  • A short message 'Auto-record settings updated' appears at the bottom right (screen 3) without leaving the list.

Avoid

  • Auto-record turns on only from the finished-meetings library (screens 1-4), but sim operators need that choice on the schedule before the session.

What it means for Essentials Recording: would sit on Center Overview or room schedule as auto-record by schedule or next session, not a bigger Record button inside the SRV.

Scoring a speaker

On Coaching playback, the coach adds a scorecard for one speaker, scores Y/N and 1-5 items with notes, submits, and sees it under the video with 'Send to Sam'.

Grade by hand or with AI (summative and formative)

Worth borrowing

  • Scorecard sits as a tab under the video (screen 1), so the coach can grade while watching.
  • Each criterion uses a 1-5 scale that turns red to orange to green, with an 'Avg. score' badge (screen 1).
  • Before scoring, the coach picks a speaker, template and who can view it (screen 3), so grading is for one learner.
  • Each item has N/A and 'Add Note', and 'Submit' stays off until answered (screens 4-7).

Avoid

  • The new-scorecard dialog covers the video while grading (screens 3-7), so faculty cannot move through the recording; keep Data Entry beside the player.

What it means for Essentials Recording: extends SRV Data Entry into a speaker-limited Scorecard tab under the player, like Abbott, with color 1-5 and send-to-learner.

WebMobbin7 steps

Generating a scorecard

From 'Scorecard Unavailable', the coach starts 'Score this call', picks a speaker, waits for generation, then reviews AI-filled 1-5 criteria with evidence notes and timestamps.

Grade by hand or with AI (summative and formative)

Worth borrowing

  • When AI does not match, the screen says so and still offers 'Score this call' (screen 1), so manual scoring stays available.
  • The coach must pick a speaker before 'Score' (screens 2-4), so one learner is graded in a multi-person recording.
  • 'Generating Scorecard' shows a progress bar and still offers 'Score this call' (screen 5), so the user is not trapped while waiting.
  • An expanded criterion shows the AI rationale and a clickable evidence time (screen 7), so the score links to a moment on the timeline.

Avoid

  • Do not auto-apply a sales-pattern scorecard when the meeting 'does not match' (screen 1), because sim rubrics must be faculty-owned checklists, not inferred call patterns.

What it means for Essentials Recording: adds AI-suggested scores with evidence timestamps into SRV Data Entry. Manual 'Score this call' maps to a rubric not auto-matched to the scenario.

VEED

Close match2 flows

VEED has the clearest recording stages: a countdown you can cancel, pause, retake and stop, then an upload. It warns clearly when the microphone is muted but still lets you record.

WebMobbin7 steps

Starting a recording

The user gets a studio ready, starts 'Record', sees a cancelable countdown, records with timer, pause, retake and stop, then opens an editor with upload progress and 'Add to project'.

Start and stop recording, by hand or automatically

Worth borrowing

  • A countdown shows 'Click anywhere to cancel' and 'Starting' before 'REC' begins (screen 2).
  • During recording, a timer sits with 'Retake', 'Pause' and 'Stop' as equal actions (screen 3).
  • When paused, the main action becomes red 'Resume' while 'Retake' and 'Stop' stay available (screen 5).
  • After stop, a review player appears with 'Uploading %' then 'Add to project' or 'Delete' (screens 6-7).

Avoid

  • A Scenes upsell dialog on pause distracts from 'Resume' and 'Stop' for operators who only need recording controls.

What it means for Essentials Recording: maps to control-room start-stop outside the SRV with countdown, pause, retake and processing after stop. The SRV stays the review place once the file exists.

Muting a microphone

On the ready-to-record screen the user opens the mic menu, chooses 'Mute Microphone', then sees 'Your microphone is muted. Unmute' and a red 'Unmute' control before 'Record'.

Start and stop recording, by hand or automaticallyCheck devices automatically

Worth borrowing

  • A warning above the stage says 'Your microphone is muted. Unmute' and can be closed (screen 3).
  • Toolbar 'Unmute' turns red with a slash while 'Record' stays available, so the warning does not block recording (screen 3).
  • The mic menu lists devices and a red 'Mute Microphone' action as an explicit choice (screen 2).

What it means for Essentials Recording: an explicit muted-mic warning before recording outside the SRV addresses audio failing at centers, without changing Transcript or Annotation tabs.

Luma

Same task, different field2 flows

Luma makes check-in the main action: scan a QR code, confirm the person, and undo straight away. It also switches between a list and the scanner, counts who is present or absent, and shows who checked each person in.

iOSMobbin8 steps

Checking in a guest

From the event home, the host opens 'Check In Guests', scans a QR, confirms 'Check In', sees success with 'Undo', then finds the guest on the Guest List.

Tag participants on the spot, by QR check-in or automatically

Worth borrowing

  • 'Check In Guests' is the main action on the session home (screen 1), so tagging comes before any recording UI.
  • After a scan, a panel shows name, email, Going status and Registered time before 'Check In' (screen 3), so the wrong person is not tagged.
  • 'Undo Check In' appears right on the success panel (screen 5), so mistakes can be fixed without leaving the scanner.
  • A list icon on the scanner (screens 2, 4, 6) falls back to the guest list when QR is not practical.

Avoid

  • An empty Invited tab with only 'No Guests' (screen 8) adds little for sim rooms, so prefer one expected-versus-present split over reply-style tabs.

What it means for Essentials Recording: QR check-in outside the SRV can label or trigger recording and feed learner names into transcript and Annotation instead of Speaker #N, without face ID.

iOSMobbin4 steps

Checking in a guest (manual check-in)

From the guest list with Going and Checked In counts, the host opens a guest card and taps 'Check In'. They see a success message and can 'Undo' with who checked them in.

Tag participants on the spot, by QR check-in or automatically

Worth borrowing

  • Going, Checked In and Not Checked In counts appear on the list (screen 1), so operators see room readiness at a glance.
  • A List | Scan switch in the bottom bar (screen 1) keeps the same roster in two input modes without leaving the screen.
  • Row badges show relative check-in time such as 'Now' or '19 min ago' (screens 1, 3), so who just arrived is clear.
  • An audit line 'Checked In · By Sam Lee' with 'Undo' (screen 4) supports multi-operator accountability and correction.

Avoid

  • Social bio and referrer details on the guest card (screens 2, 4) are noise for faculty, so keep identity and roster status only.

What it means for Essentials Recording: a per-room roster with List|Scan check-in replaces ad-hoc name entry, and the Checked In set becomes the participant list on the recording.

Preply

Same task, different field1 flow

Preply's device self-test ends in a clear result: a 5-second audio and video sample, a Yes/No check with a way to fix problems, and a final checklist.

WebMobbin7 steps

Testing devices

Before 'Enter classroom', the learner opens 'Test devices', records a short audio and video (AV) sample, answers Yes/No about seeing themselves, then returns with Camera and mic checkmarked.

Check devices automatically

Worth borrowing

  • The device-check screen splits Camera and mic from Network and device, with tips on how to fix problems (screen 2).
  • A 5-second AV sample says it will not be saved or shared and starts with 'Start test' (screen 3).
  • During the sample the screen shows 'Recording in progress', 'Try saying…', and a progress bar (screen 5).
  • Yes/No asks 'Can you see yourself' with 'If not, we'll help you fix it' and 'New test', then Camera and mic get green checks (screens 6-7).

Avoid

  • The device-check screen repeats (screens 2 and 4) with little new information, which confuses operators running a daily room self-test.

What it means for Essentials Recording: replaces the planned per-room self-test outside the SRV with a guided cam/mic sample, Yes/No confirm and checkmarked health summary before the session.

Devices

From Home favorites, the user opens Devices, scans room Groups and a device list, and sees health from unresponsive to Online, On or Off.

Manage many rooms at onceCheck devices automatically

Worth borrowing

  • Room Groups such as Bedroom sit above the flat device list (screen 2), so the user jumps by place before scanning endpoints.
  • A red dot and 'Device is unresponsive' under the device name (screen 2) show the problem without opening the device.
  • Controllable devices show On/Off badges while always-on devices show Offline/Online text (screens 3-4), matching how each device works.

Avoid

  • Dashed 'Shop' and Suggested Favorite cards (screens 1-2) clutter the health overview with commerce placeholders.

Creating an announcement

From Communication, the user opens 'Announce', writes text, uses voice, or picks a sound preset, sends, and gets confirmation that the message reached all supported devices.

Send announcements to the room or simulator, live or automatic

Worth borrowing

  • 'Announce' and 'Drop In' are separate top actions (screen 1), because one-way broadcast and live intercom are different controls.
  • Keyboard, Sounds and Popular tabs sit under one compose screen (screens 2-3), so the user can type, speak or pick a cue without leaving.
  • One-tap sound presets and an 'Add Sounds' list with preview play (screens 2-3) give stock cues for common room prompts.
  • After send, 'Announced to all supported devices' plus 'New Announcement' (screen 5) proves delivery and lets the user repeat.

Avoid

  • The flow broadcasts to 'all supported devices' with no room or device picker (screen 5), but Essentials needs explicit room versus simulator (manikin) targets.

What it means for Essentials Recording: shapes the announcement panel outside the SRV as compose then confirm delivery; Essentials should add room versus simulator targets before send.

Slack

Same task, different field2 flows

Slack shows both kinds of announcement. Push-to-talk is its own mode, with a large button you hold down, and a scheduled message can't be published until a recipient is set.

iOSMobbin4 steps

Turning on push-to-talk

In a live huddle, the user turns on push-to-talk from 'More options' and then talks by holding down a large button instead of using the normal mute.

Send announcements to the room or simulator, live or automatic

Worth borrowing

  • Push-to-talk is a mode you switch on during a session (screen 1), not a permanent replacement for mute.
  • While push-to-talk is on, a crossed-out microphone, a 'Push-to-talk' label and an X to exit make it clear you are not live yet (screen 2).
  • A large button at the bottom of the screen lets the user talk without looking for a tiny icon (screens 3 to 4).
  • Rings pulse around the microphone button while it is held, so the user knows the channel is open (screen 4).

Avoid

  • Push-to-talk is hidden under 'More' (screen 1), but faculty who talk into rooms need room or simulator audio one tap away.

What it means for Essentials Recording: a model for talking into the room or as the voice of the manikin from beside the SRV, with a hold-to-talk button that clearly shows when you are live.

WebMobbin5 steps

Creating a workflow

From Slack's workflow templates, the user sets up a daily standup message at a fixed time, can't publish until a recipient is chosen, and saves the message after previewing it.

Send announcements to the room or simulator, live or automatic

Worth borrowing

  • Templates are grouped by what starts them, such as 'Scheduled date & time' (screen 1), so operators pick a trigger instead of starting from scratch.
  • A step with no recipient is marked pink with 'Needs attention' and can't be saved (screens 2 to 3), so an announcement with no target can't go out.
  • Both the trigger and each following step have an 'Edit' link (screens 2 and 5), so the user can change the time or target without starting over.
  • A preview before 'Publish' shows the exact wording that will be played in the room (screens 4 to 5).

Avoid

  • A general workflow builder with many steps is too much for a single scheduled room message, compared with a simple form for time, target and message.

What it means for Essentials Recording: useful for scheduled announcements, the 5 am self-test and automatic recording outside the SRV. Each needs a time, a required target and a preview.

Fireflies fills in AI notes and a live transcript during the recording. A 'Catch me up' button helps faculty who looked away, and selecting text pins a single bookmark star on the timeline.

Live notes

From Home, the user opens Live Notes on a LIVE banner, sees AI Notes still writing plus AskFred shortcuts, then works a live Transcript with 'REC' and assists.

Add faculty notes and automatic markers

Worth borrowing

  • A global LIVE banner shows session title, start time, 'Live Notes' and 'Stop' (screen 1), so recording is visible outside the player.
  • AI Notes say 'writing notes… points will appear here automatically' (screen 2) while speech-to-text works.
  • 'Catch me up (Last 1 min)' and related assists (screens 2-3) help faculty re-enter without jumping through the video.

What it means for Essentials Recording: would add live Annotation and Transcript to the SRV and a Center Overview LIVE strip, with AI markers during the session and Catch-me-up for faculty who stepped away.

Partiful

Same task, different field1 flow

Partiful asks for confirmation, with a safe way to cancel, before reversing a check-in, so a wrong participant tag is undone on purpose rather than by an accidental tap.

iOSMobbin3 steps

Cancelling a check in

On 'Check In Guests', tapping a checked-in guest's checkmark opens 'Uncheck them?'; confirming 'Undo check-in' returns them to a 'Check in' button like unchecked guests.

Tag participants on the spot, by QR check-in or automatically

Worth borrowing

  • A filled checkmark versus outlined 'Check in' (screen 1) makes presence readable without opening a card.
  • A confirm titled 'Uncheck them?' shows the guest avatar and name before 'Undo check-in' (screen 2), so reversing a tag is deliberate.
  • 'Nevermind' sits beside 'Undo' (screen 2), so accidental taps can be cancelled safely.
  • Search 'Find a guest…' above the list (screen 1) scales when many learners are on the roster.

Avoid

  • Reply-to-invitation (RSVP) emoji lines such as Going or Maybe (screens 1-3) set a party tone; sim rooms need role or group instead.

What it means for Essentials Recording: adds confirm-before-untag for room check-in outside the SRV so wrong learner tags can be reversed without rewriting Annotation or transcript speaker labels by hand.

Wellfound

Same task, different field1 flow

Wellfound has a summative scorecard with a four-step scale, a switch to show earlier scorecards, and a view once it is submitted. It is mainly useful as a contrast to Grain, which scores each criterion separately.

WebMobbin6 steps

Adding a scorecard

A recruiter opens a candidate overview, adds a Project scorecard with free-text notes and Strong Yes to Strong No, then sees 'Scorecard Submitted' with the saved Strong Yes card.

Grade by hand or with AI (summative and formative)

Worth borrowing

  • An empty Scorecards screen offers 'Add scorecard for [name]' (screen 2).
  • A footer rating strip shows Strong Yes, Yes, No and Strong No in color (screen 3).
  • 'View all previous scorecards' sits above the form (screen 3).
  • A success banner 'Scorecard Submitted!' then a list card shows reviewer, Strong Yes and the note (screen 6).

Avoid

  • A free-text-only scorecard with no checklist criteria fits SRV grading worse than an Abbott-style checklist with timestamps.

What it means for Essentials Recording: extends SRV Data Entry with a right-rail scorecard, a final four-step scale and confirmation, but lacks evidence timestamps and rubric rows.

Tesla

Outside idea1 flow

Tesla picks a camera by its position on a diagram of the car, with a wedge showing what each camera sees. Live video only appears in a special mode. It suggests picking room cameras by position.

iOSMobbin2 steps

Live camera

From Security & Drivers with Sentry Mode on, the user opens 'View live camera' and sees one live feed, a vehicle diagram of camera positions, Honk/Flash, and a record control.

New PTZ camera controls and 360° cameras

Worth borrowing

  • Sentry Mode must be ON before 'View live camera' (screen 1), so live view only opens when monitoring is already on.
  • A floor-plan style map shows position dots and view wedges around the subject (screen 2), so the user picks a camera by place, not by a cryptic device name.
  • A single live preview sits above the map (screen 2), so cameras switch without leaving the monitoring screen.
  • A grid control beside the map (screen 2) shortcuts toward a multi-angle layout from the same picker.

Avoid

  • Honk and Flash on the camera screen (screen 2) are the wrong metaphor for sim rooms; keep space for PTZ, presets or room/simulator announce instead.

What it means for Essentials Recording: informs Center Overview and a simplified camera picker: a room diagram with camera dots to switch the live feed, not continuous PTZ and no face ID.

Halide Mark III

Outside idea1 flow

Halide offers a few fixed, labeled zoom levels instead of a continuous slider. That is a zoom-only model for simpler PTZ.

iOSMobbin2 steps

Changing a focal length

In Halide's viewfinder the user switches labeled zoom stops from 1x to 2x, with no pan, tilt or continuous zoom control.

New PTZ camera controls and 360° cameras

Worth borrowing

  • Labeled stops (.5, 1x, 2) replace a continuous zoom slider (screen 1).
  • The active stop fills yellow (screen 2), so current magnification is obvious.

Avoid

  • Do not treat this as full PTZ, because the screens show only labeled zoom stops with no pan, tilt, presets or click-to-point.

What it means for Essentials Recording: informs simplified zoom outside or beside SRV live view with labeled stops for faculty. It does not replace a 360 flatten or PTZ joystick.
